title: Reliability guarantee ledger entry
description: One entry in a factory's guarantee ledger: a precise claim, the owner accountable for it, the mechanism that provides it, the oracle that would catch its violation, and the current evidence status. The ledger's ground rule: documentation alone never raises the status; only an enforcing mechanism in the running system, or a passing fault drill, does.

id.description: Stable identifier of the guarantee, upper case with hyphens, for example AUTH-STALE-PUBLISH. Referenced from reviews, drills, and incident write-ups; never reused for a different claim.

claim.description: A precise safety or liveness statement over the whole system, not over one component. 'The workflow engine recovers' is a component property; 'one logical work item has at most one authorized writer at a time' is a factory claim.

owner.description: Team or person accountable for keeping the claim true and for keeping its evidence current.

mechanism.description: The mechanism that provides the guarantee, and the identities or facts it consumes. Naming the inputs makes it checkable that the mechanism sees the identities the claim is about.

type.description: Mechanism family, for example destination-fence, destination-deduplication, lease-and-generation, content-addressed-publication.

items.description: One identity or fact the mechanism consumes, named as a field from the factory contract.

inputs.description: Identities and facts the mechanism consumes, for example [claim_generation, work_id].

oracle.description: The check that would catch the claim being false. An oracle that cannot fail is not an oracle; where a negative control exists, the assertion states what the control is expected to do.

type.description: Check family, for example fault-drill, readback-comparison, invariant-monitor.

assertion.description: The machine-checkable condition, stated over observable facts: what must hold after the scenario runs, and what the negative control must violate when one exists.

evidence.description: Current evidence backing the claim. Statuses only move up with evidence, and they decay: an enforced mechanism that was refactored, or a drill that has not run since the system changed, warrants demotion.

status.description: declared: the claim is written down and nothing checks it. enforced: a mechanism in the running system rejects violations. fault-tested: a drill injected the fault, the oracle caught the violation on the negative control, and the protected arm passed.

drill.description: Path or name of the drill that exercises the fault. Expected for fault-tested entries; states exactly which failure was injected and where.

last_verified.description: Absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD) the evidence was last produced or re-run. An old date is a prompt to re-drill, not a permanent credential.

artifact.description: Path to preserved evidence backing the status, for example an ordered event journal from the drill run. Evidence directories are append-only by convention.
